t: Introduction and overview — C-17 Globemaster III
name: Introduction and overview — C-17 Globemaster III — aircraft record
title: Introduction and overview — C-17 Globemaster III
description: Introduction and overview of the C-17 Globemaster III: What this aircraft is, its role, and why it matters in aviation history. The C-17 Globemaster III is a four-engine strategic airlifter built by McDonnell Douglas (now Boeing), entering service in 1995. It carries outsized cargo — including main battle tanks — into short, austere airfields. 279 were built for the U.S. Air Force and allies including the UK, Australia, Canada, and India. Baseline facts: Four-engine strategic airlifter; service from 1995; 279 built; carries tanks into austere fields..
how_it_works: Wings generate lift from airflow; the engine provides thrust; control surfaces and fly-by-wire or mechanical controls steer the aircraft in three axes.
key_points: C-17 Globemaster III: What this aircraft is, its role, and why it matters in aviation history.
Four-engine strategic airlifter; service from 1995; 279 built; carries tanks into austere fields.
Key figure: 170,900-lb payload; four Pratt & Whitney F117 turbofans; short-field capability.
